findings.text: `check_source_results` now runs outside the damaged-evidence wrapper. It reads `setupOutcomes`, `setupResults`, `setupErrors` and `trace[-1]["primaryCode"]` (in `upstream_fidelity.check_results`), but `validate_fields` never checks those fields. A damaged corpus record now raises a bare `KeyError`, `IndexError` or `TypeError` that does not name the case or give a recovery action, and the `try` removed at `corpus_shards.py:82` used to catch exactly these errors. A length mismatch in those fields (the `ValueError` from `zip(..., strict=True)`) also gets the wrong label: "Native fidelity difference ... Exclude this source assertion" instead of the recapture advice. Fix: wrap `KeyError`, `TypeError` and `IndexError` from `check_source_results` as damaged binding evidence with the recapture message (or check those fields in `validate_fields` first), and add a test where a Tcl record is missing `setupResults`.
